key_insight: A non-planar 3×3 Josephson crossbar qubit can realize a flux-tunable Z3 combinatorial gauge symmetry, opening a route to engineered gauge physics in circuit QED.
engineering_relevance: This geometry expands superconducting-qubit design beyond planar layouts, potentially enabling scalable lattice-gauge simulators and new hardware architectures for quantum simulation.
method: Built a 3×3 crossbar Josephson array inside a superconducting cavity
Tuned magnetic flux to probe and control Z3 gauge symmetry
Compared measured excitation spectra with a neural-network-generated variational quantum state model
evidence_signal: The measured excitation spectrum closely matches neural-network predictions, and the observed fine-structure splittings near the CGS point are consistent with weak tunneling or small symmetry-breaking imperfections.
watch_item: The symmetry features are sensitive to residual tunneling and fabrication/experimental imperfections, which could limit clean realization of the ideal CGS point.
paper_title: Nonplanar qubit with tunable gauge symmetry
